In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the GABAergic system in cerebellar FN is involved in the regulation of the stress response, and the GABAA receptors in cerebellar fastigiatal nucleus may be involved in the regulation and control of gastric mucosal damage induced by stress.

the results of the present study suggest that microinjection of a GABAA receptor activator muscimol in cerebellar FN exacerbates the stress-induced gastric injury, which may involve the activation of the greater spheric nerve and the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis, and the inhibition of gastric mucosal blood supply and antioxidant capacity.
the results of the study are important for the treatment of patients with gastric diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cerebellum is involved in the regulation of gastric function through cerebello-hypo-thalamic circuits.
the cerebellum may participate in the regulation of gastric mucosal damage through the hypothalamus.

GABAA receptor activation in FN is involved in the stress-induced gastric injury, and the mechanism is mediated by the activation of the cerebello-hyothalamic circuit, which increases the gastric acid secretion and reduces the gastric mucosal perfusion, and further decreases the proliferation and increases the apoptosis in the gastric mucosal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cerebellar FN is a new site for stress-induced gastric mucosaldamage and that the cerebello-hypothalamic pathway plays an important role in the pathogenesis of stress-induced gastric injury.
the cerebellum is a brain structure that has been largely overlooked when it comes to the regulation of the gastrointestinal system.
the fastigial nucleus plays an important role in the regulation of gastric mucosal damage under stress, and this regulation may involve the cerebello-hypo-thalamo-limbic system.
